overview: The Cornish Seal Sanctuary is a rescue centre beside the Helford River at Gweek, run by the SEA LIFE Trust charity, and it’s a gentle, feel-good visit. Its main job is nursing sick and orphaned grey seal pups found around the Cornish coast back to health and releasing them; most years it takes in several dozen, mainly between September and March.

As well as pups in recovery, there are permanent residents that can’t go back to the wild, including grey seals and a little colony of puffins. The sanctuary started in 1958 when its founder rescued a stranded pup near St Agnes, and moved here in 1975.

expect.title: The seal hospital
expect.text: Peek into the hospital and nursery pools to see pups at different stages, from close care to learning to compete for fish before release. Autumn and winter, during pup season, is when it’s busiest.

expect.title: Resident seals
expect.text: The permanent residents live in bigger outdoor pools. Catch a seal talk to hear their stories, and watch them swim through the underwater viewing windows.

expect.title: Puffin Island
expect.text: Ten puffins that can’t be released because of old injuries live in their own habitat, having come from the charity’s sister sanctuary in Iceland.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Entry is paid, but keep your receipt: it gets you back in free for 12 months. Booking ahead is advised.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: Recent hours have been 11am to 4pm, last entry 3pm; check before you go, as they change with the season.

goodToKnow.label: Children
goodToKnow.text: Under-17s need to be with an adult aged 18 or over.

goodToKnow.label: Weather
goodToKnow.text: Most of it is outdoors around open-air pools, so dress for the weather.

week.text: An easy, unhurried couple of hours that suits younger children, especially in pup season. It’s at the head of the Helford River, so you can combine it with the creeks and gardens of the Helford or a trip down onto the Lizard.
